description: We are a team passionate about software development, data analysis, and space technology. Our goal is to develop an interactive web application that integrates NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite data to analyze wildfire activity, identify historical patterns, and detect unusual fire conditions. We aim to transform scientific data into accessible and useful information that supports environmental monitoring and wildfire prevention.
summary:
ENTALPIA is a web platform that turns NASA satellite data into wildfire prevention for Mexico. It pulls heat detections from the NASA FIRMS API: VIIRS NOAA-21 in near real time for a live interactive map, plus two years of MODIS and VIIRS NOAA-20 records for history. Because the two sensors see fire at different resolutions (1 km vs. 375 m), we harmonize them onto a common scale so their records can be compared fairly. A burn-activity calendar then highlights when and where fire is most frequent and flags statistically unusual days. A logistic regression model, trained on brightness, fire radiative power and other detection features, estimates how likely each hotspot is a real fire. The data refreshes automatically every three hours.

Data alone does not prevent fires, so ENTALPIA also teaches. It includes prevention guides and "Don't Let Entalphy," a browser game where players race the clock to remove fire hazards from a house.

Most fires are caused by people, which means most can be prevented. ENTALPIA makes satellite data understandable and actionable for communities, students and local authorities.
details:
What it does

ENTALPIA is a web platform that turns NASA satellite fire data into prevention information for Mexico and its surroundings. It has four main parts:

  • Live fire map: every three hours, the server downloads the latest VIIRS NOAA-21 heat detections from the NASA FIRMS API and draws them on an interactive map.
  • Burn-activity calendar: we keep a two-year history of MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS NOAA-20 detections. Users can pick any area by typing its coordinates and see, day by day, when and where fire activity is highest.
  • Fire classification model: a logistic regression model uses detection features (location, brightness temperatures, pixel size, fire radiative power and day/night) to estimate how likely each hotspot is a real fire. On held-out data it reached a balanced accuracy of 98.2% and an ROC AUC of 0.99.
  • Prevention and education: guides on how to prevent fires, a community survey with live charts, and “Don’t Let Entalphy,” a browser game. Players have three minutes to make a house safe across five rooms: blowing out candles, unplugging overloaded extension cords, turning off the stove and heater, checking the smoke detector, moving a gasoline can and closing the grill.

How it works

MODIS and VIIRS cannot be compared directly. VIIRS pixels are 375 m and MODIS pixels are about 1 km, so one fire appears as several VIIRS points but only one MODIS point. We harmonize them in three steps:

  1. We assign every detection to a 0.01° (~1 km) grid cell and count burning cells instead of points.
  2. On days both sensors observed, we compute a scaling factor k = Σ MODIS cells / Σ VIIRS cells, and use it to convert VIIRS into “MODIS-equivalent” values.
  3. We average the available sensors into a single daily series.

To flag unusual days, we compare each day with all other days of the same month using a z-score. Days with z ≥ 2 are marked as unusual, which is fewer than about 2.5% of days under a normal distribution.

Tools and technologies

  • Python 3 with pandas, scikit-learn (logistic regression), folium (interactive maps) and matplotlib
  • SQLite for the fire history and user accounts
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the website; the game runs on an HTML5 Canvas with pixel art drawn entirely in code
  • NASA FIRMS API (VIIRS NOAA-21, VIIRS NOAA-20 and MODIS, both near-real-time and standard processing)
  • Google Forms and Google Sheets for the survey
  • GitHub for version control and Render for hosting

Benefits and intended impact

Most wildfires are caused by people, so most can be prevented. ENTALPIA turns raw satellite data that is hard to read into maps, calendars and clear explanations. Communities and local authorities can see when fire risk peaks in their area and plan ahead. The game reaches children and families, teaching prevention habits at home through play instead of lectures.

What makes it creative

ENTALPIA connects space-based observation with everyday action. The same platform shows a fire detected from orbit and teaches someone to unplug an overloaded extension cord. The harmonization of two satellite generations into one comparable record is our own method. The game turns prevention into a challenge against the clock.

Factors we considered

  • Accessibility: a simple interface in Spanish that anyone can open from a browser, with no installation needed.
  • Scientific honesty: we harmonize the two sensors instead of simply adding their points, and we report margins and confidence levels instead of exaggerating results.
  • Class imbalance: most detections in our data are real fires, so a model that always answers “fire” would already score high on accuracy. That is why we evaluate it with balanced accuracy and AUC instead of accuracy alone.
  • Privacy: passwords are stored as hashes, sessions use secure cookies, and the survey is anonymous.
  • Low cost: the platform uses free and open data, open-source libraries and free hosting.
